A.explanation: The leftward and downward forces meet at the bottom edge, but the north-east force extended backward passes to the left of that point, so the three lines are not concurrent.

B.explanation: The rightward, downward and up-left forces can all meet at one common point below the centre, so both resultant force and resultant moment can be zero.

C.explanation: The rightward force at the top and the downward force at the centre meet near the top, but the south-east force at the bottom-right corner cannot pass backward through that same point.

D.explanation: The two upward forces are parallel to each other and opposite to the downward force, so the lines cannot meet at one point and a moment balance is not possible with this symmetric spacing.

hints: Extend the line of each arrow in both directions and look for where the three lines of action cross on each block.
Recall that three non-parallel coplanar forces in equilibrium must be concurrent - all three lines must pass through the same point so there is no resultant moment.
Check the backward extension of the diagonal force in A and B toward the crossing of the horizontal and vertical forces at the bottom edge to see which one passes through it.
walkthrough: Identify the two conditions for equilibrium: vector sum of forces $= 0$ and sum of moments about any point $= 0$.
For three non-parallel coplanar forces, the moment condition means the three lines of action must be concurrent - they must all intersect at one common point.

In each diagram locate the intersection of the horizontal and vertical forces. In A and B the horizontal force acts along the bottom edge and the vertical force acts downward through the centre, so they meet at the centre of the bottom edge.
Extend the diagonal force backward. In B the up-left force points away from that bottom-centre point, so its backward direction runs down-right straight toward it and all three lines can meet.

In A the up-right force extended backward runs down-left and misses that bottom-centre point to the left, in C the three extensions do not share one point, and in D the forces are parallel so they cannot be concurrent.
Only B allows both a closed force triangle and zero moment by suitable magnitudes, so the block could be in equilibrium. This is option B.
